questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-renewable energy resource?
questions.explanation: Natural gas is a fossil fuel that takes millions of years to form, making it non-renewable. Once used, it cannot be replaced within a human lifetime. Solar, wind, and tidal energy are all renewable because they are constantly replenished by natural processes.

questions.stem: A town needs a reliable energy supply that works at all times, day and night, regardless of weather. Which resource would be LEAST suitable?
questions.explanation: Solar panels only generate electricity during daylight and their output depends on weather and season, making them unreliable as a sole power source. Nuclear, natural gas, and geothermal power stations can operate continuously regardless of weather conditions. This is a key disadvantage of solar energy for baseload power.

questions.stem: Wind turbines are an example of a renewable energy resource. Which is a valid disadvantage of wind power?

options.text: They produce greenhouse gases during operation
They generate electricity intermittently, depending on wind conditions
They use up a non-renewable fuel source

questions.explanation: Wind turbines only generate electricity when the wind blows, making their output variable and unpredictable. They do not produce greenhouse gases during operation (only during manufacture), do not use fuel, and do not produce radioactive waste. This intermittency means backup power sources are needed.

questions.stem: A hydroelectric power station generates 2 MW of electrical power. If the station operates at 80% efficiency, what is the rate at which gravitational potential energy of the water is lost?
questions.explanation: Efficiency = useful output / total input. Rearranging: total input = useful output / efficiency = 2 / 0.80 = 2.5 MW. The GPE lost per second (input power) is 2.5 MW, of which 2 MW becomes electrical energy and 0.5 MW is wasted. Option A incorrectly multiplies output by efficiency.

questions.stem: Which statement best explains why many countries use a mix of energy resources rather than relying on just one?

options.text: Each resource produces a different type of electricity
A mix provides reliability, since renewable sources are intermittent and fossil fuels are finite
It is cheaper to build many small power stations than one large one
Different energy resources produce energy at different voltages

questions.explanation: An energy mix provides security of supply. Renewable sources like wind and solar are intermittent (weather-dependent), so fossil fuels or nuclear provide baseload power. Fossil fuels are finite, so renewables help reduce dependence on them and cut carbon emissions. All power stations produce the same type of electricity at standardised voltages.
